Production-ready: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, and other serving frameworks have adopted KV cache quantization inspired by this work
 Practical impact: Directly increases the max batch size and sequence length you can serve on a given GPU [...] Pairs with PagedAttention: KIVI reduces per-block memory, PagedAttention reduces fragmentation, both are needed for production LLM serving
 In system design: cite when asked about serving LLMs at scale, long-context support, or reducing per-request memory cost [...] ### Key Idea

During LLM inference, the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length and batch size, often becoming the primary memory bottleneck. KIVI observes that keys and values have fundamentally different outlier distributions: keys have large-magnitude outlier channels (columns) that persist across all tokens, while values have large-magnitude outlier tokens (rows) that affect all channels. This asymmetry motivates different quantization strategies for K and V.

# TurboQuant-vLLM: A Practical KV Cache Quantization Solution for Large Model Inference

This article introduces the TurboQuant-vLLM project, a KV cache compression solution integrating Google TurboQuant, KIVI asymmetric quantization, and Bonsai 1-bit technology. It can compress the 32K context KV cache of Llama-3.1-8B from 4GB to 1GB, saving 74% of memory while maintaining 99.4% attention fidelity.

No. They target KV cache rather than model weights. In many deployments, cache quantization and weight quantization are complementary.

What should I compare first for deployment?+

Compare total memory, achieved throughput, and quality on your real prompts. Paper headline numbers alone are not enough for deployment decisions.

Sources

Google Research →TurboQuant paper →KIVI paper → [...] ## How to choose in practice

01

### Check your real bottleneck

If weights dominate memory, KV cache quantization may not move deployment economics much. If long contexts dominate, both methods become more relevant.

02

### Check implementation availability

A theoretically better paper result is not enough if your runtime stack does not ship kernels or maintenance support for that method.

03

### Benchmark on your own workloads [...] TurboQuant

Google frames TurboQuant as a broader vector quantization method for both KV cache and vector search, with low overhead and near-optimal distortion claims.

KIVI

KIVI is a tuning-free asymmetric 2-bit KV cache quantization method focused specifically on inference memory and throughput.
